title: Self-healing traffic gate with prognostic rollback scheduler
author: Priya Suresh
description: Motivation: We observed incident patterns where a small regression in an A/B arm degraded user experience slowly and only surfaced after sustained traffic. This PR adds a prognostic rollback scheduler and a self-healing traffic gate that combines short-horizon telemetry forecasting, a conservative anomaly scorer, and lightweight replay/bisect workflows so the system can proactively hold or revert risky promotes before widespread impact.  Summary of changes: implemented a prognostic score pipeline that consumes recent SLO/time-series windows and outputs a short-term risk forecast; added TrafficGate controller that enforces holdpoints when forecasted risk crosses policy thresholds; built a rescue-oracle that can run fast replay of recent 1% samples in a sandbox to validate rollback decisions; added operator-visible "rescue" and "replay" actions to Redwood Console so on-call can review diagnostics and trigger manual rescue if needed; introduced feature-flagging and gradual enablement config under rollout.policy.prognostic.enabled=false by default.  Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-4421) [x] unit + integration tests for forecast scorer [x] smoke tests for traffic gate hold/open actions [x] e2e replay against local-capture harness [x] console UI surfaced and smoke validated  Implementation notes: forecasting uses a lightweight ARIMA-like exponential smoother tuned for short windows to avoid model drift; anomaly scorer penalizes latency regressions higher than minor fidelity deltas; the rescue-oracle runs isolated synchronous replay (max 30s) and returns a scalar pass/fail + diff snapshot used to justify automated rollback.  Rollout plan: behind feature flag in main, enable in staging for 48h with canary percent=2% then roll to 10% with manual checks; enable prognostic auto-hold only after 7d stable metrics.  Related: supports both canary and A/B lanes and hooks into existing rollout audit logs and snapshotting.  Why different: unlike prior reactive rollback controllers, this one uses short-term prognostic signals and a bounded replay verification step to reduce false-positive auto-rollbacks.  Links: Linear ENG-4421 (design), SUP-1723 (support ticket that motivated fast replay).

review_comments: Diego Morales: Nice approach on the short-horizon forecasting. Concern: false positives may still trigger a hold. Can we add an entropy-based cooldown so multiple non-overlapping anomalies are required before auto-hold?
Priya Suresh: Added entropy cooldown in the policy (policy_schema.yaml) with conservative defaults and tests showing reduced false positives. See commit b7d2e41.

Ava Chen: Please add a simulation that replays historical incidents to prove the prognostic thresholds reduce incident blast radius. Also request: metric tags should be consistent with observability conventions.
Priya Suresh: Added historical incident simulation harness and adjusted tags to use service.namespace and rollout.id. See test/integration/replay_harness_test.go and telemetry changes.
Liam O'Neill: Minor nit: console button copy should say 'Request rescue replay' not 'Rescue'. Fixed. Also add a guard so replay cannot run for >30s to protect hosts.
Priya Suresh: Addressed both nits; replay timeout enforced in replay_oracle.go and UI copy updated.
release_notes: Added prognostic rollback scheduler and self-healing traffic gate with conservative defaults; feature-flagged under rollout.policy.prognostic.enabled; Console now shows 'Request rescue replay' action for operator verification.
post_merge_tasks: - Monitor ENG-4421 canary dashboard for false positives for 14 days. - Add policy presets for enterprise customers (follow-up ENG-4488). - Announce feature-flag rollout and ops runbook.
notes_for_release: This is opt-in via rollout.policy.prognostic.enabled=false. Recommend staged enablement per PR rollout plan. No breaking changes.
incident_reference: SUP-1723: customer reported slow-degrading A/B arm that wasn't caught by threshold-based alerts; motivated replay harness development.
